title: Center-Borne Days after a Lapsed Certification on Coinsurance Paid from Resident Funds
content:
Days after a lapsed certification are provider liable and never billed to the resident. In the return of a coinsurance overcharge paid from a Resident Trust Fund Accounts account, the block's owed days are reduced by **the block's center-borne days**, which follow the certifications on the resident's episode under Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage:

| Episode and block records | Center-borne days |
|---|---|
| the coverage office has reversed days of the block as uncertified days | those days |
| no certification is recorded on the episode after its coverage start date, and the initial recertification day has passed | the block's days after that day, through the covered end |
| otherwise | none |

The initial recertification day is the covered-day number the episode's coverage sets for the first physician recertification, counting the coverage start date as day 1; it has passed once today is later than that day.

## Hypothetical illustration

The episode's initial recertification day is day 14 and its coverage start date is 2 March, so that day is 15 March. A block runs 2 to 31 March with a covered end of 31 March; today is 3 April.

| Records | Center-borne days |
|---|---|
| 4 days of the block reversed as uncertified days | 4 |
| no reversal; no certification recorded after 2 March | 16 (16 to 31 March) |
| no reversal; a certification recorded on 14 March | none |
